paper.title: Coordination without communication: optimal regret in two players multi-armed bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Two-player cooperative stochastic three-armed bandit with collisions (no communication)
unmapped: Losses (not rewards); colliding players both suffer loss 1 and observe 1 (collision not revealed)
Players cannot communicate; regret compared with the sum of the two smallest mean losses
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t=1, \hdots, T$, Alice and Bob choose independently two actions $i_t^A \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $i_t^B \in \{1,2,3\}$. If they collide, i.e. $i_t^A = i_t^B$, then they both suffer the maximal loss of $1$. Otherwise they respectively suffer the losses $\ell_t(i_t^A)$ and $\ell_t(i_t^B)$. As is usual in bandit scenarios, each player receives only its own loss as feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Full-information toy model (two players, three arms, independent loss sequences)
unmapped: Each player observes its own independent i.i.d. loss vector for all arms, regardless of collisions (no implicit communication)
Collisions still cost loss 1 but are not observed
settings.definition_quote: When player $X \in \{A,B\}$ plays action $i$, they observe the loss $\ell_t^X(i)$ (irrespective of the other player's action). ... For this modified model we assume such a full information feedback.

unmapped: Each player observes its own independent i.i.d. loss vector for all arms; collisions not observed

Full-information partition strategy with dynamic interface (derandomized)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: There exists a randomized strategy (with shared randomness) for Alice and Bob such that, for any $\p \in [0,1]^3$, we simultaneously have \[ \E [R_T] \leq 2^{20} \sqrt{T \log(T)} \, \] and \P ( \forall t \in [T], i_t^A \neq i_t^B ) \geq 1-\frac{1}{T}

results.notes: R_T defined with mean losses, so pseudo-regret. Comparator is the best pair of arms. Expectation over losses and shared randomness.
Bound on the probability that at least one collision ever occurs; holds simultaneously with the regret bound.

source.label: thm:add
source.quote: There exists a deterministic strategy for Alice and Bob such that, with probability at least $1- \Omega(1/T)$, \[ R_T = O(\sqrt{T \log(T)}) \,. \]

results.notes: Probability stated as 1-Ω(1/T) (presumably 1-O(1/T)). Strategy uses collisions for implicit communication; number of collisions O(sqrt(T log T)) w.h.p.

source.label: thm:toyupper
source.quote: There exists a deterministic strategy for Alice and Bob in the full-information toy model such that with probability at least $1-1/T$, one has both: R_T \leq 320 \sqrt{T \log(T)} \,, and $\forall t \in [T], i_t^A \neq i_t^B$.

results.notes: Probability 1-1/T. Also guarantees no collision at all on that event. Deterministic version via dynamic interface; constant 320 proved for the randomized version, derandomized argument sketched.

conditions: specific prior over p on a circle of radius ~T^{-eps} around (1/2,1/2,1/2), reinforced near ties

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $c>0$ and a distribution over $\p$ such that, for any strategy in the full-information toy model, one has: \[ \E_{\p} R_T \geq c \sqrt{T \log(T)} \,. \]

results.notes: Universal constant c; expectation over p drawn from a constructed distribution. Holds for the toy model only, not transferred to the bandit problem.
